title: Canary contract enforcer with graceful fallback and warm-start probes for private control plane upgrades
creator: Priya Menon
description: Problem: Our current private control plane canary process occasionally allows a canary promotion to proceed even when subtle contract regressions occur (schema changes in APIs, soft timeouts in health-checks, KV cache incompatibilities). This leads to post-promotion rollbacks and manual mitigation. Goal: implement an automated 'canary contract enforcer' that evaluates a set of syntactic and behavioral contracts during staged promotions and enforces graceful fallback (automated pause + tenant quiesce + rollback) if contracts are violated. Additionally, integrate a warm-start probe for KV/stateful caches to avoid cold-cache false positives.
background: We already run staged canary promotions with traffic slicing, smoke tests and synthetic probes. Recent incidents indicate gaps: 1) API response shape drift (nullable fields removed) passed current checks because smoke datasets didn't exercise edge shapes; 2) KV warmup required for certain tenants was not accounted for, causing transient error spikes after promotion; 3) rollback windows are sometimes too late because the gating checks are not contract-aware. This ticket adds contract enforcement and a warm-start probe phase to the canary pipeline and wires it into Terraform-driven promotion flows for private/VPC control planes.
acceptance_criteria: Canary pipeline runs contract checks (schema + semantic) against a configurable contract bundle before each promotion wave
If a contract fails, the pipeline automatically pauses promotion, routes new canary traffic to fallback model (previous control plane), and notifies on-call with remediation steps
Warm-start probe stage runs KV/cache warmup for configured tenant cohorts and verifies latency/error baselines before allowing promotion to the next wave
Terraform IaC modules expose configuration for contract bundles, warm-start cohorts, pause/rollback thresholds and notification hooks
End-to-end test harness with simulated contract regression and cache-warmup failure demonstrating automatic pause and rollback
Telemetry and dashboards show contract check pass/fail rate, warm-start success rate, and time-to-rollback metrics
implementation_notes: Add a new 'contract-enforcer' component in the control plane promotion orchestrator that accepts a bundle (JSONSchema + behavioral checks as tests) and runs it against a canary instance
Define a lightweight DSL for behavioral checks (e.g., response-time quantiles, top-level field presence, enum set validation) that can be extended by the research team
Introduce a 'warm-start' probe runner that replays curated KV-prefill scripts and measures synthetic request latencies against tenant cohorts
Update Terraform modules (private/controlplane/modules/promotion) to accept configuration flags: contract_bundle_uri, warmstart_cohorts, pause_thresholds, notification_hook_arn
Implement a bounded pause window: when contract check fails, promotion pauses for 'pause_window_seconds' and triggers auto-rollback if unresolved
Expose feature flags to gate rollout of enforcement per-region and per-tenant for gradual rollout
risks: False positives from overly strict contract rules could unnecessarily stall safe promotions; need conservative defaults and easy overrides
Warm-start scripts could take significant time for large tenants; must limit cohort size and provide async warm-start where possible
Terraform module changes require coordination with on-prem/offline customers who manage their own IaC; clear upgrade notes required
Behavioral check DSL complexity may increase maintenance burden; keep initial DSL minimal
notes: This ticket intentionally separates syntactic schema checks from heavier semantic regression tests. Start with JSONSchema bundles authored by product and design, and iterate the behavioral DSL in subsequent sprints.
